subject: Transportation Systems
title: Accessibility in Transit
description: A quick, practical guide to Accessibility in Transit.

hook.text: A transit system that a wheelchair user can't board isn't a public system. It's an exclusive one.

buildup.text: Low-floor buses, platform-level boarding, and elevator access make transit usable for everyone.

discovery.text: Accessible design helps more than disabled riders—parents with strollers, elderly travelers, injured commuters.

twist.text: Retrofitting old stations with elevators costs millions per station. Many cities are decades behind.

climax.text: New York's subway has 472 stations. Less than a third are fully accessible. The retrofit will take 30 years.

punchline.text: Accessible transit isn't a luxury. It's the bare minimum.

quiz.question: Why is transit accessibility slow to implement in old systems?
options: Retrofitting stations with elevators costs millions each
